seoTitle: Fix 'Inventory Not Tracked' in Shopify or Stop Tracking
metaDescription: Understand why Shopify shows 'Inventory not tracked,' how to enable tracking for real stock counts, and how to disable it for unlimited items.
intro: Seeing 'Not tracked' next to a location in Shopify's inventory panel throws a lot of store owners, especially when they expected to see a quantity and a low-stock warning instead. It isn't a bug — it's a per-variant setting that's simply switched off. This guide shows exactly where that setting lives on the product page, what it looks like in both states, and how to decide which products should actually have stock counts turned on versus left open-ended.

steps.heading: Start from your Shopify admin home
steps.body: Log in and land on the admin Home screen, which summarizes sessions, orders, and payments to capture for the last 30 days. This isn't where inventory settings live, but it's the fastest route to Products in the left-hand menu, and it's worth a glance anyway — an order sitting in "1 order to fulfill" is often the moment someone notices a product let itself be sold with zero stock, which is exactly the untracked-inventory scenario this guide fixes.

image.caption: The Shopify admin Home dashboard, with Products one click away in the left-hand navigation.

steps.heading: Open the product that's showing the issue
steps.body: From Products, click into the specific listing — here, a phone case product with its title, description, and media already filled in. Scroll down past pricing to the Inventory section; that's the block that controls whether Shopify counts stock for this specific product, separate from everything else on the page like pricing, shipping weight, or the description editor above it.

image.caption: A product's edit page in Shopify admin. The Inventory section further down the page is where tracking gets turned on or off.

steps.heading: Recognize the untracked state
steps.body: In the Inventory section, an unchecked "Track quantity" box is the whole story: no Quantity field appears, and under Location the store simply reads "Not tracked" instead of a number. This is Shopify's default for a lot of import and duplication flows, which is why products can end up in this state without anyone deliberately choosing it. If a product should be showing stock counts and isn't, this checkbox is the first thing to check.

image.caption: The Inventory section with Track quantity unchecked. No quantity field shows, and the location reads "Not tracked."

steps.heading: Turn on tracking and set your quantity behavior
steps.body: Check Track quantity and the panel expands into a real quantity table, broken down by location into Unavailable, Committed, Available, and On hand counts. A second checkbox, "Continue selling when out of stock," appears right below it — leave that off if you want the product to actually go unavailable at zero, or check it if you're fine taking orders that get fulfilled once more stock arrives. Shopify is explicit that this setting won't affect Shopify POS staff, who'll see a warning but can still complete the sale.

image.caption: Track quantity enabled, showing the per-location quantity breakdown and the option to keep selling once stock hits zero.

steps.heading: Decide which products should stay untracked
steps.body: Not every product needs a stock count. Digital downloads, made-to-order items, and services have no physical inventory to run out of, so leaving Track quantity off for them is correct, not a mistake to fix. The goal isn't to track everything — it's to make sure the setting matches how you actually fulfill each product, so a physical item with limited stock never accidentally sells past what you have.

steps.heading: Audit your catalog for defaults left unchanged
steps.body: Once you understand the toggle, it's worth a pass through your full product list checking that tracked and untracked items were set intentionally rather than left on whatever Shopify defaulted to during import or duplication. A quick way to spot problems is watching for products that sell out instantly with no warning, or conversely items you know are limited that never seem to go unavailable — both point back to this same Inventory section.

faq.question: Why does Shopify say a product's inventory isn't tracked?
faq.answer: It means tracking was never turned on for that variant, so Shopify isn't counting stock levels or triggering sold-out states for it.

faq.question: Should I track inventory for every product?
faq.answer: Not necessarily; physical stock items usually benefit from tracking, while digital products or unlimited-supply items are often better left untracked.

faq.question: Will turning off inventory tracking let customers order out-of-stock items?
faq.answer: Yes, untracked products stay purchasable regardless of how many you actually have, which is the point for unlimited-availability items.

faq.question: Can I turn inventory tracking back on after disabling it?
faq.answer: Yes, you can toggle tracking on or off for a product at any time from its inventory settings.
